handback.t:
### Spec Compliance
✅ Host gains `session: { messages, id }`. `toChatMsgs` maps engine rows to `ChatMsg` with only role, text and tool names (`hooks/chat-msg.ts:29-31`). The call is the bare `$.session.messages()`, so it reads the main conversation only. That matches the `SessionMessagesCall` overload `(): Promise<SessionMessage[]>` in the d.ts. `hostOf` is exported (`register.ts:43`) and `chat-host.spec.ts` covers the mapping, the leak check and the no-argument call. I did not re-run the suites, per instructions.
⚠️ One doc/behavior mismatch, listed under Minor.

Named risks:
- **(a) Required `Host.session`: no typecheck break found.** I grepped all of `plugins/ruflo-console` for `: Host`, `): Host`, `as Host` and `satisfies Host`. Every test fake and fixture that is typed as Host is built with `... as unknown as Host`. That includes `mission-control.spec.ts:37`, `fixtures/mission-cli-real.ts:117`, `fixtures/live-console.ts:36`, `fixtures/sessions-world.ts:35` and the `(): Host => ({...}) as unknown as Host` helpers in `wf-anatole`, `wf-templates` and `wf-worktrees-view`. The `hostOf` in `ap-live.ts:88` and `wf-convo-live.ts:57` just look up an existing Host. The only literal Host built from `$` is `register.ts:hostOf`, which now supplies `session`. Making the member required is safe for upstream `scripts/typecheck.sh`.
- **(b) Privacy: no leak found.**
  - The mapper builds a fresh object with exactly three fields. It never touches `toolResults`, `handle`, tool `input`, tool `result`, tool `text` or `agentId`.
  - Per the d.ts, a user message's `text` is "its text blocks joined; '' when it has none". Tool-result bodies live in the separate `toolResults` array, not in `text`, so they cannot enter through the user `text`.
  - The test seeds a SECRET in `toolResults`, `toolUses[].result` and `toolUses[].text`, plus a file path and an input value. It asserts none appear in the JSON and that the keys are exactly `role`, `text`, `tools`.
  - `text` still carries whatever the person or assistant typed or pasted. That is the conversation itself, and ADR-486 constrains what later tasks may do with it.
- **(c) Field names match the d.ts.** `SessionMessage.role/text/toolUses` and `ToolUseSummary.tool` are used correctly. `tool` is the right field; `ToolUseSummary` has no `name`.
- **(d) `export` on `hostOf`: no side effect.** `register.ts` has only two exports, `hostOf` and `register`. `register` is the plugin entry export and its signature is unchanged. The report says the validator still passes; I did not re-run it.

### Strengths
- Whitelist-style mapping, so new engine fields cannot leak by default.
- The privacy test is a real mutation target: sentinel secrets in every field that must be dropped, plus a key-set equality assertion.
- Minimal diff, no new dependencies or network calls. Types come from `claude-code`, and the module's own `ChatMsg` type is exported for later tasks.
- The no-argument call is asserted (`calls` equals `[[]]`), which pins the main-session-only rule.

### Issues
#### Critical
None.
#### Important
None.
#### Minor
1. `host.ts:62` says "the newest turns", but `toChatMsgs` returns every row, unbounded and unsorted. Either drop the claim or add a tail limit before a later task renders or sends this.
2. `chat-msg.ts:30` calls `row.toolUses.map` on a field the d.ts types as required. If the engine ever omits it on a user row, the whole call throws. `(row.toolUses ?? [])` would cost nothing. The host contract already says callers catch refusals.
3. `ChatMsg.text` and tool names are raw, unsanitised engine strings. That is fine for this task. Later tasks must pass anything handed to a model through `modelLine`, per the global constraint.

### Assessment
**Task quality:** Approved
**Reasoning:** The mapper copies only role, text and tool names, and its field names match the d.ts. Every Host fake in the repo is cast with `as unknown as Host`, so the required member does not break upstream typecheck. The three Minor items are polish.
